name: UGC 7346 (Hubble)
blurb: UGC 7346, a dwarf galaxy shaped by the merger of two smaller dwarfs, seen by Hubble.
label: ugc7346-hubble
story: Faint streams and shells around this dwarf galaxy at the edge of the Virgo Cluster record a recent merger of two dwarfs, and its globular clusters crowd toward its center. Astronomers think they may be sinking together to build a nucleus, and Hubble looked to catch a nuclear star cluster in formation.

claims.text: UGC 7346 is a dwarf galaxy in the peripheral regions of the Virgo Cluster
UGC 7346 is catalogued as a dwarf elliptical, low surface brightness galaxy
Diffuse streams or shells around UGC 7346 suggest a recent merger of two dwarf galaxies
Its globular cluster candidates are highly concentrated toward the galaxy's center
The globular clusters may be collapsing to form a nuclear star cluster; the Hubble program aims to observe nuclear star cluster formation in UGC 7346
